title: Quiet Loop
user: Adult language learners who want a sustainable 10-minute review habit without streaks, feeds, or punitive notifications.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A solo language-app maker asks whether deliberately avoiding gamification, streaks, subscriptions, and engagement tricks is commercially viable; the thread contains 67 comments.
A reviewer asks for an Archive action because a card can stop being useful while the source note remains valuable.

recurrence: Two separate 2025–26 learning-tool communities identify the same retention risk: engagement mechanics and endless review queues make a tool less useful, not more. The HN discussion is substantial (67 comments).
current_workaround: Use Duolingo/Anki despite unwanted mechanics, turn off notifications, or abandon stale cards manually.
incumbents_and_gap: Duolingo optimizes habit loops and Anki optimizes scheduling; neither makes a calm, finite daily routine with first-class card retirement its main product promise.
smallest_useful_product: A local-first PWA with one bounded daily set, optional weekly planning, a one-tap archive-with-reason action, and exportable CSV. Non-goals: a language course, social feed, generated lessons, or streaks.
success_measure: In a 30-day pilot, 50% of activated users complete at least 12 sessions without enabling a streak or push notification, and 30% archive or revise an obsolete item.
monetization: one-time — the audience explicitly values an unpressured, subscription-free learning environment.
constraints: Store learning data on device by default; provide export/delete; do not imply pedagogical outcomes; accessibility must include keyboard-only review.
why_distinct: It is a deliberately finite review ritual and content-retirement tool, rather than another gamified language app or an Anki clone.
